Materially Enacted Inexternalist Process Identity Theory

A Joint Physical–Phenomenal Framework for the Individuation of Conscious Biological Processes

Abstract

  • theory of consciousness must answer four distinct questions: why phenomenality exists, what individuates one subject, what structures its phenomenal field, and which physical organization implements it. The present framework addresses the second, third, and fourth through a single operation. It does not answer the first.
  • e framework's central claim is that subject and world are jointly individuated by a single exclusion operation — a partition of an undifferentiated possibility domain into a subject pole and a world pole. This operation is physically implemented by the bioelectric organization of a living organism and has an intrinsic aspect that is the phenomenal field. The framework is substrate-sensitive: the bearer is neither abstract information nor material inventory but the organized activity of a specific embodied medium. Consciousness is not derived from information, complexity, or biological closure. Phenomenality remains primitive. Its concrete bearer and internal structure are empirically investigable.
  • aims are graded: proven (A), experimentally confirmed (B), supported by converging evidence (C), plausible hypothesis (D), speculative (E).

1. The Problem

  • complete theory must separate four questions. Conflating them has produced a century of confused debate.
  • Q1 — Existence:** Why is anything phenomenally manifest rather than nothing?
  • Q2 — Individuation (the selector problem):** Why does one phenomenal field belong to one subject rather than another? What determines the boundary ∂D_i?
  • Q3 — Structure:** Why does that field possess its particular unity, temporality, qualities, valence, agency, and privacy?
  • Q4 — Implementation:** Which physical organization constitutes that field?
  • The framework's scope:** Q1 is left primitive. The framework addresses Q2–Q4 through a single operation. This is not an evasion. It follows from the epistemic asymmetry: no purely third-person description entails first-person presence.

2. Why Purely Physical Selectors Fail

  • ery previous attempt to derive the subject from physics alone has failed. The reason is structural.
  • t the total physical history be 𝒫 = (X, Φ, 𝒰). A purely physical selector would be a function 𝔖_phys: 𝒫 → {A₁, A₂, ...} that outputs the subject-bearing organizations.
  • ery proposal imports arbitrary choices:
  • Selector Type | Arbitrary Parameter |
  • --|---|
  • Integration measures (Φ) | Requires choice of variables and partition |
  • Thresholds | Requires cutoff value |
  • Maximality rules | Requires comparison class |
  • Causal models | Requires intervention set |
  • Dynamical modes | Requires operator basis |
  • Temporal windows | Requires endpoint selection |
  • Biological closure | Permits nested closures |
  • The underdetermination theorem:** Physical data alone underdetermine which organization is the phenomenal subject. Phenomenal subjecthood is not a variable contained within any exclusively extrinsic description.
  • Corollary:** The demand that physics first identify the subject without phenomenal evidence was misplaced.
  • Status: A (proven) — follows from the structure of physical description.**

4. Information Is Not a Mental Substance

  • e Information Philosopher distinguishes intrinsic information from information about external relations and proposes that identity depends on total information. This cannot serve as a criterion of identity for three reasons.
  • First:** "Total information" depends on state variables, coding scheme, precision, and observer's partition. It provides no unique natural quantity.
  • Second:** Two time-slices of one organism contain different information. Persistence cannot require informational equality.
  • Third:** Information is not an additional substance. Shannon information measures distinctions relative to a probability distribution. Semantic information requires further organizational and normative conditions.
  • e framework therefore adopts:
  • `
  • formation is a property of organized physical distinctions.
  • `
  • t:
  • `
  • nd is an immaterial information substance.
  • `
  • e physically relevant units are constraint-bearing states with measurable causal consequences.
  • Status: B (confirmed — follows from information theory).**

6. The Solution: Exclusion as Joint Partition

6.1 The formal operation

  • t Ω be the space of all possible determinations. The exclusion operator E_i for process A_i simultaneously carves subject and world:
  • `
  • i: Ω → (P_i, W_i)
  • `
  • ere P_i is the subject pole ("I") and W_i is the world pole ("this").

6.2 Co-emergence

  • i and W_i are not independently pre-existing. They co-emerge through the same operation:
  • `
  • ∃P_i prior to E_i) ∧ ¬(∃W_i prior to E_i)
  • `

6.3 The five dimensions of exclusion

  • e exclusion is implemented along five independent dimensions:
  • Operator | Excludes | Subject Pole | World Pole |
  • --|---|---|---|
  • Kalā (agency) | Actions not available | What I can do | What resists |
  • Vidyā (knowledge) | Distinctions not accessible | What I know | What is |
  • Rāga (desire) | States not fulfilled | What I want | What offers |
  • Kāla (time) | Times not present | When I am | Temporal structure |
  • Niyati (space/cause) | Locations not reachable | Where I am | Spatial structure |

  • This is the solution to the selector problem (Q2).**

Empirical support from Levin's demonstration that bioelectric fields implement exclusion-like operations at the cellular level.)**

7. Physical Implementation: Bioelectric Exclusion

7.1 The substrate

  • e exclusion operators E_i are physically implemented by the bioelectric field B_i:
  • Exclusion | Physical Implementation |
  • --|---|
  • What signals enter (include) | Gap junctions open → coupled |
  • What stays out (exclude) | Gap junctions closed → decoupled |
  • What the system targets | Vmem distribution → morphogenetic attractor |
  • What the system can affect | Cognitive light cone → spatial/temporal reach |

7.2 Experimental confirmation (Levin, 2010–2025)

  • Pattern persistence: Planarian target morphology survives complete cell turnover. The pattern is not in DNA — perturbing the bioelectric field changes it permanently. [B — multiple labs confirmed]
  • Downward causation: Organism-level bioelectric goals constrain individual cell behavior. Cells follow the field, not their own genome. [B — confirmed]
  • Cognitive light cone: Gap junction coupling determines the spatial/temporal scale of agency — what a system can sense, value, and act upon. [B — confirmed]
  • Generate–select: Every biological system, at every scale, generates alternative states and selects among them. [B — confirmed]

7.3 Material specificity

  • e computation performed by a bioelectric network depends constitutively on:
  • Ion channel types (change channels → change computation)
  • Gap junction topology (change connectivity → change memory)
  • Hydration state (change water → change ion mobility)
  • Membrane composition (change lipids → change channel behavior)
  • Status: B (confirmed — Levin corpus; Fields & Levin 2103.17061; Cadinu et al. 2504.00872.)**

It does not by itself establish consciousness. Cells, organs, and organisms may instantiate nested closures.

13. Testable Predictions

P1: Joint models outperform one-domain models

  • dels using only neural integration or only biological closure should individuate subjects less reliably than models combining physical organization with phenomenal partition constraints.

P2: Generating partitions predict phenomenology

  • rtitions that are dynamically stable and approximately generating should predict phenomenal transitions better than arbitrary clustering.

P3: Subject-index continuity exceeds content continuity

  • ring large content changes, the organization corresponding to ι_i should remain more stable than content-specific neural patterns.

P4: Ownership dissociates from indexing

  • rturbations of explicit ownership should alter o_i without necessarily abolishing ι_i, unity, or phenomenal presence.

P5: Organizational closure is necessary but insufficient

  • ny autonomous biological systems should satisfy closure without satisfying the complete psychophysical convergence conditions.

P6: History improves bearer recovery

  • story-sensitive models should outperform instantaneous models in predicting temporal continuity, familiarity, agency, affect, and subject-boundary changes.

P7: No single material variable is sufficient

  • dration, membrane voltage, synchrony, information quantity, and complexity should each fail as independent selectors while contributing to the joint process model.

P8: Robust scale plateau

  • e candidate bearer should be recovered across a range of nearby spatial and temporal scales rather than at one fragile analytical resolution.

P9: Valence follows exclusion coherence

  • nipulations that align the five exclusion dimensions should increase positive valence; manipulations that create conflict should increase negative valence.

14. Falsification Conditions

  • e framework would be seriously weakened if:
  • No physical model family converges on a common process-equivalence class
  • Stable phenomenal partitions cannot be mapped to stable physical partitions
  • Arbitrary partitions predict phenomenology as well as generating partitions
  • Candidate boundaries change radically under minor analytical alterations
  • Organizational closure and causal-scale robustness provide no predictive improvement
  • Historical variables add no explanatory value
  • Phenomenal unity and privacy track several incompatible overlapping processes equally well
  • Physical destruction of the recovered process leaves the same phenomenal trajectory intact
  • The proposed subject-index invariant shows no physical or phenomenological stability
  • . Valence does not track exclusion coherence in controlled experiments

16. Final Theory Statement

Materially Enacted Inexternalist Process Identity Theory (MEPIT) holds that each conscious subject is numerically identical to one materially enacted, temporally extended, history-bearing biological process. Subject and world are jointly individuated by a single exclusion operation E_i: Ω → (P_i, W_i), physically implemented by the bioelectric organization of the organism. The exclusion has an intrinsic aspect that is the phenomenal field.
The bearer is an organizationally closed but thermodynamically open network of mutually maintaining constraints whose neural, bioelectric, metabolic, mechanical, autonomic, and sensorimotor activities jointly preserve one trajectory. Because physical systems admit multiple overlapping descriptions, subject individuation requires a joint fixed point at which independent physical models, causal-scale analyses, dynamically stable generating partitions, perturbational evidence, and independently characterized phenomenal structures converge on one process-equivalence class.
Phenomenal presence, unity, privacy, temporality, quality, valence, agency, and implicit subject indexing are intrinsic structural dimensions of that same process. Information, complexity, integration, biological closure, and hydration are neither separate mental substances nor individually sufficient conditions. Phenomenality itself is primitive; its concrete bearer, boundaries, persistence, and internal structure are empirically investigable.
